 New Report Opens Door for Atlanta Braves to Reunite With 3-Time All-Star in Blockbuster Trade
 Jason Burgos 
 Nov 4, 2026 
 · 
 3 min read

 A new report opens the door for the Atlanta Braves to reunite with one of their homegrown stars in an unlikely blockbuster trade, if they are willing to pay the price.
 After a 2025 season that ended in their first playoff miss in eight years, the Braves were motivated for a big bounceback this year, and they had the pieces to do it. Despite dealing with key injuries early in the season and a disappointing year from top star Ronald Acuna Jr., Atlanta was back in the postseason this fall after winning the National League East for the seventh time in the last decade.
 Go Ad-Free 
 Yet, when they came face-to-face with the defending champion Los Angeles Dodgers in the Divisional Round, they were folded up and sent home in just four games. Despite the disappointment, they still had one of the best records in baseball and are not far off from being a serious title contender in 2027.
 If they want to be in the Fall Classic next year, they could use another high-impact talent in the starting rotation alongside 2026 Cy Young candidate Chris Sale. Well, they could get that in a reunion with a former All-Star.
 Go Ad-Free 
 Could an Atlanta Braves reunion with Max Fried happen this offseason?
 Sep 22, 2026; Bronx, New York, USA; New York Yankees starting pitcher Max Fried (54) reacts during the fifth inning against the Tampa Bay Rays at Yankee Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Brad Penner-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect 
 According to ESPN’s Kiley McDaniel, “ the Yankees are thinking about ” taking a run at signing two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal in free agency this month. The MLB insider then added that if New York were to land the ace, they would follow up by “trading from their pitching stockpile.”
 The Yankees could certainly look at trading players like Luis Gil, Clarke Schmidt, or Will Warren. However, with a salary cap, or something close to it, expected to arrive in the next collective bargaining agreement, they will need to offload a lot of money if they were to give Skubal a contract worth around $400 million. Moving the six years and $189 million still owed to Fried would go a long way in helping balance their payroll. 
 The Braves would have liked to keep the three-time All-Star two offseasons ago, but the price was just too high. However, if the Yankees are willing to pick up around $8 million of the $31.5 million he makes annually until 2032, it would make his contract far more reasonable.
 The former Atlanta prospect has been very good the last two seasons and would be a strong No. 2 behind Sal. He would also be a short-term ace option if the 37-year-old called it a career soon. The Braves have a solid minor league system and could certainly offer talent the Yankees would be interested in.
 A lot has to happen first before this is a real possibility. However, if the Yankees are in on Skubal, Braves fans could benefit if New York wins the sweepstakes.
